questions.q: What stays constant across nearly all S3 storage classes, even as cost and retrieval time change?
options: The 11-nines durability guarantee
The retrieval time
The storage price per GB
Nothing — durability drops as you move down the ladder
questions.explain: Every class from S3 Standard down to Deep Archive carries the same 11-nines durability guarantee — you're trading retrieval speed and cost, not data safety.

questions.q: What does S3 Intelligent-Tiering do that Standard-IA does not?
options: Automatically moves objects between access tiers based on observed usage, without you predicting the pattern up front
Guarantees faster retrieval than S3 Standard
Eliminates the storage cost entirely
Requires manual lifecycle rules to change tiers
questions.explain: Intelligent-Tiering monitors actual access and automatically shifts objects between frequent- and infrequent-access tiers, unlike Standard-IA which is a fixed manual choice.

questions.q: Roughly how long can retrieval take from S3 Glacier Deep Archive?
options: Up to 12 hours
Milliseconds
Always under 1 minute
Retrieval is not possible once archived
questions.explain: Glacier Deep Archive is the coldest, cheapest tier and can take up to 12 hours to retrieve — appropriate for long-term compliance data rarely, if ever, accessed.

questions.q: What does a lifecycle policy do?
options: Automatically transitions or expires objects between storage classes based on age, without manual intervention
Encrypts objects automatically after a set number of days
Prevents objects from ever being deleted
Converts object file formats automatically over time
questions.explain: A lifecycle policy is a bucket/prefix rule set that automatically moves objects to cheaper storage classes (or deletes them) as they age, without manual cleanup.

questions.q: Why might a team choose Standard-IA over S3 Standard for a dataset?
options: The data is accessed infrequently but still needs millisecond access when it is accessed, and lower storage cost is worth a per-GB retrieval fee
Standard-IA has faster retrieval than S3 Standard
Standard-IA has no durability guarantee, so it's used only for disposable data
Standard-IA is required for any object larger than 1 GB
questions.explain: Standard-IA trades a lower storage price for a per-GB retrieval fee, while still keeping millisecond access — appropriate for infrequently accessed but still latency-sensitive data.
